To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the relevance of a group identity influences the way in which people cope with collective disadvantages and that the relevance of the group identity influences the psychological mechanisms of collective coping with collective disadvantages.

group identity's relevance to group members moderates the psychological mechanisms that predict collective action: when group identity is relevant, group-based anger predicts collective action, but when group identity is less salient, group-efficacious beliefs predict collective action.

(1) when the group identity of disadvantaged group members is relevant, they cope with their group's disadvantage more through emotion-focused coping (i.e., anger about their group disadvantage), and this increases their collective action tendency; and (2) when their group identity is not relevant, they cope more instrumentally with their disadvantage (i.e., group-efficacy), and this is predictive of their collective action tendency.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the relevance of identity to collective action can be enhanced and how this relevance affects the two psychological mechanisms of coping with collective action.
how people cope with their group-based disadvantage and how they decide to act to change it.
how people cope with the experience of collective disadvantage, and how this coping process relates to collective action tendencies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the relevance of a group identity influences how people cope with their group's disadvantage and that it is a key determinant of collective action.
when group identity becomes less relevant, people are less likely to experience group-based anger, and they are more likely to focus on the efficacy of collective action.
the relevance of identity is an essential prerequisite of the emotion-focused coping mechanism, and it is a necessary condition of the problem-focused coping mechanism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the relevance of identity is a crucial determinant of how people respond to collective disadvantage.
the relevance of the group identity is a key moderator of collective action.
the relevance of identity moderates the psychological mechanisms of collective actions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the relevance of a group identity influences how people cope with a group disadvantage and hence whether they will engage in collective action to improve the group's situation.
the relevance of collective identity influences how people cope with group disadvantage, which in turn influences their collective action tendencies.
when group identity becomes less relevant to group members, they tend to focus on whether they can effectively solve the problem of their disadvantage, rather than whether they are angry about it.
